This is a genre that I've only recently got into (and can't seem to get out of), so my list will be small:

The following 3 games claim no AI at all:

Shelves & Sorcery: Tidy up the Enchanted Shop.
Black Friday Janitor: Clean the Whole Mall (very big with over 30,000 items!)
Put Back Stuff.

The following two games used some AI:

Cleaning Up the Puzzle Gallery. AI was used for code, but not images, music, artwork, etc.
Megastore: Tidy Up Together. AI was used for some content, but reviewed and edited by humans.

Both of these games have high positive reviews, so it depends on whether you can be a bit forgiving or totally unforgiving!

There's quite a lot of these sorting games around now, so do a search and see what takes your fancy. Some games will have an AI disclosure statement on the store page, or you can find information via reviews and discussion boards.

I have not found any other game similar in intelligence, humor and charm as 'Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library!', with or without GenAI use. 'Shelve the Potions' is the closest so far and I do recommend it but, due to the simplistic nature of the shelving (color based) and puzzles, even it fell short. Possibly there might be others out in time - I have big hopes for 'Tidy Up History' which is coming out today and 'Alchemess: Tidy Up Your Potion Shop!' which is coming out tomorrow - but we will have to see.

However, if you just looking for other tidy-up games, there are a slew available at this time, plenty more coming out down the pipe and, since they have to state on their steam store page whethere or they use GenAI, you can easily garner that information for yourself. Also, you might be interested to know there are external tools you can use to track and filter Steam games that disclose using GenAI or you can utilize Steam's 'ignored text filters' tool.

Here is a list of 'tidy-up' games someone in the 'Arcane Library' discussion forum posted. They found it by selecting tag Organizing and, in sub-genre, picking Collectathon:

https://store.steampowered.com/tags/en/Organizing?facets13268=0%3A4%2C2%3A29&offset=48

Originally posted by 1ostcat:

Whoa, disliking art created using AI is a social justice issue now? Crazy times.
I hate that too, but the fact that they literally state the art was all created by people actually does indicate that the art was, in fact, not created by AI. Just in case you weren't sure.

What they did state was that they used AI to refine it AFTER human creation. And people do that all the time without even calling it AI. I have personally used an online tool to resize photos for posters and stuff because it wasn't something I could do on my own. Loads of people use editing software on their selfies and other pictures to clear up blurry bits or lighten the area, or even outright alter things. These things have been happening since before the thieving GenAI came on the scene, but nobody required disclosure back then because nobody cared. We also all used spell check, grammar check, and google translate as needed and nobody cared....but now when people declare these things for a game everyone freaks out.

I will avoid games that use only AI to create the art/music, and AI voice acting (because that sounds so awful). But refinement? Editing? That is absolutely nothing new, and if you weren't freaking out at developers in the past telling them to hire editors and whatnot, then it is hypocritical.

I don't know where people in these discussions are getting "GenAI" from. The description said they used AI. AI has been around for 50 years and includes a lot of technology we've been using for decades, but I assume devs now have to say whenever they use any of that tech because of all the abuse of LLMs. It looks like all they used were some filters and a spelling/grammar checker. That's not GenAI. Generative AI is AI that generates new content out of the whole cloth, it is not a process that modifies or makes suggestions for existing content. Those are different things.
